mosca_framework.description: Dr. Michele Mosca's Theorem for Quantum Risk: If Data Lifetime (X) + Migration Time (Y) > Quantum Horizon (Z), then information will be exposed to quantum adversaries before migration can complete.
mosca_framework.horizon_notes: Configurable assumption representing expected emergence of a Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC).

classification_rules.description: Public-key key establishment or asymmetric encryption subject to Store-Now-Decrypt-Later
classification_rules.rationale: Adversaries can record ciphertext today and decrypt retroactively once CRQC is realized.

classification_rules.description: Public-key digital signatures used for authentication and code signing
classification_rules.rationale: CRQC will forge digital signatures, compromising identity verification and software integrity.

classification_rules.description: Classically broken cryptographic primitives (MD5, SHA-1, 3DES, DES)
classification_rules.rationale: Primitive has known classical collision or cryptanalytic attacks regardless of quantum timeline.

classification_rules.description: 128-bit symmetric ciphers vulnerable to Grover search halving security margin to 64 bits
classification_rules.rationale: Grover's algorithm reduces effective security from 128 to 64 bits. Upgrade to 256 bits recommended.

classification_rules.description: 256-bit symmetric ciphers retain >= 128 bits post-quantum security
classification_rules.rationale: 256-bit key provides 128-bit quantum security against Grover's algorithm, satisfying NIST PQC requirements.

classification_rules.description: SHA-256 and SHA-3 family hash functions retain adequate quantum collision margin
classification_rules.rationale: Standard cryptographic hashes of >= 256 bits provide sufficient preimage and collision resistance under quantum algorithms.
